You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Two concurrent redemptions of the same token can both succeed, because the check and the write aren't under one lock.

Rules:

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Single-use is not atomic. `redeem_reset_token` checks `record["used"]`, then sets it, with no lock. Unwidened, 8 threads on one token gave exactly 1 success in 20 rounds (the window is narrow). With a 0.01 s sleep between check and write in a scratch copy, every round gave 8 successes. Fix: a `threading.Lock` held across the lookup, check, and set.
- [minor] Non-finite timestamps are not validated. `issue_reset_token("ada", now=float("nan"))` then `redeem(..., now=1e9)` returns "ada", so the token never expires. `now=-inf` at issue makes the token expire at once. Not in the criteria; reproduced.
- [minor] Expiry is judged per attempt, not sticky. Redeem at 9000 raises TokenExpired, then redeem at 1500 on the same token succeeds. This matches the literal "more than 1800 s after issue" wording and the skew rule, so I flag it only for the orchestrator to decide (see OPEN QUESTIONS).
- [minor] `test_now_zero_is_honoured` never asserts that redeeming at `now=0` succeeds, only that a later redeem expires. Add a `redeem(token, now=0)` success assertion.
- [minor] No validation of `now` types. `issue_reset_token("ada", now="5")` is accepted and stored; redeem would then fail with a TypeError rather than an InvalidToken. Not reproduced past the issue step.
- [minor] `_TOKENS` is never pruned, so memory grows with every issued token. Pre-existing, not introduced by this diff.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- issue_reset_token(username, now=None) and redeem_reset_token(token, now=None); `now` is a Unix timestamp in seconds; when None it defaults to time.time() evaluated at call time (not at def/import time).
  - Hostile: now=0 must be used as 0, not replaced by time.time() (no `now or time.time()`); float timestamps work.
- A token redeemed more than 1800 s after issue raises TokenExpired. Redeeming at exactly issued+1800 succeeds; issued+1800.001 (or +1801) raises TokenExpired.
  - Hostile: issue with explicit now and redeem with explicit now far in the past (clock skew, now < issued) — must not raise TokenExpired.
- Tokens are single-use: after one successful redemption, redeeming the same token again raises TokenUsed (also when the second attempt is past the expiry window — TokenUsed is checked before expiry).
  - An expired redemption attempt does not count as a use: redeeming an expired token again still raises TokenExpired, not TokenUsed.
  - Concurrent redemptions of one token: exactly one succeeds.
- TokenExpired and TokenUsed are subclasses of InvalidToken, exported from shop.auth; unknown tokens still raise InvalidToken (a plain InvalidToken, not TokenExpired/TokenUsed).
